methods.intended_use: A declared base series multiplied period by period by a declared seasonal index.
A declared amount repeated over periods and stepped by a declared rate at a declared period.
Revenue per period from days open, an average ticket and declared daily transactions.
The total of declared cost or funding lines and the total of each declared category.
How many periods the declared cash flows need to recover a declared investment, interpolated within the recovery period.
Value a stream of cash flows at a user-supplied discount rate.
The discount rate at which a declared stream of cash flows has a net present value of zero (the IRR, for conventional cash flows).
How many periods the discounted cash flows need to recover a declared initial outlay, interpolated within the recovery period.
Units needed to cover fixed cost at a constant unit contribution, with the break-even revenue, contribution margin, margin of safety and target-profit volume when those inputs are declared.
Linear association between two numeric variables in a sample, with interval, p-value and effect size.
Monotone association between two variables, robust to outliers and skew; fallback for Pearson.
Linear association of one numeric outcome with up to five numeric predictors, with intervals, p-values and effect sizes.
Linear regression with HC3 heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors; fallback for OLS.
Compare the means of two independent groups on a numeric outcome, with interval, p-value and standardized effect size.
Compare two independent groups without assuming normality; fallback for Welch.
Summarize one numeric variable in a dataset (n, missing, mean, median, range, sample SD).
Compare the means of three or more independent groups with an omnibus F test, an eta-squared effect size and per-group summaries.
Compare three or more independent groups without assuming normality; nonparametric fallback for one-way ANOVA.
Test whether two categorical variables are independent from a table of observed counts, with a Cramer's V effect size.
Project a linear trend in a single time series forward for a user-chosen horizon, with prediction intervals and a disclosed out-of-sample error on the recent past.
Compute liquidity, profitability, solvency and efficiency ratios from figures on your own financial statements, showing each ratio's declared formula and the figures it used.
Adjust a pre-declared family of p-values for multiple testing with Holm's step-down or Bonferroni, and count how many remain significant at a declared alpha.
Plan a two-sample or one-sample comparison of means: the power for a stated effect, and the minimum detectable effect at a declared target power, under the normal approximation.

Report how much of a variable is missing and bound the complete-data mean under the worst case: every missing value at the observed minimum or maximum, with the missing-data mechanism recorded as the owner's declaration.
Compare two matched measurements on the same observations (for example before and after) using the mean within-pair difference, with a confidence interval, a paired t test and Cohen's dz.
Compare one sample mean with a declared reference value, with a confidence interval, a one-sample t test and Cohen's d.
Binary logistic regression (0/1 outcome) with up to five numeric predictors: coefficients as log-odds, odds ratios, Wald p-values and a McFadden pseudo R-squared.
Cronbach's alpha for the internal consistency of a set of items answered by the same respondents.
Discounted cost-benefit appraisal: present values of declared costs and benefits, the net present value and the benefit-cost ratio.
Cost-effectiveness analysis against a declared comparator: incremental cost per unit of effect (ICER) for each other option, with dominance flags.
Social return on investment: present value of declared social benefits divided by the declared investment.
Unit contribution margin, payback of the acquisition cost and (when a churn rate is declared) a period-value LTV and LTV/CAC.
Break-even in units and revenue for a fixed product mix: the mix-weighted contribution margin and the per-product break-even quantities.
Two-way balanced factorial ANOVA on one numeric response: the two main effects and their interaction, with F tests and partial eta-squared.
Compare every pair of independent groups with a Welch t-test and a declared family-wise correction (Holm, Bonferroni or none), reporting raw and adjusted p-values.
Convert an amount from one ISO 4217 currency to another at a rate the owner declares, recording the rate, its provenance, any source and date.
Compute the weighted average cost of capital from declared market values of equity and debt and declared costs of equity and AFTER-TAX debt.

Discount a declared stream of free cash flows at a declared rate and declared timing (end-of-period, or an explicit mid-year convention), with an optional Gordon-growth terminal value, to an enterprise value.
Bridge a declared enterprise value to an equity value by subtracting net debt (debt minus cash) and the declared minority and preferred claims, with an optional per-share value.
Summarize a variable under declared design or frequency weights: weighted mean, weighted standard deviation, effective sample size and design effect.

Run a declarative management-accounts engagement (chart, opening balances, entries and schedules) through the ledger kernel: statements, trial balance, two-route cash flow, closing and the retained-earnings rollforward, with every invariant checked.
Compare a student's own trial balance with the one rebuilt from their own journal: every line that matches, differs or has no counterpart, with candidate causes labelled as heuristics.
Find the future value of a lump sum plus a level payment, the present value of those payments, and the effective annual rate, showing the periodic rate and number of periods used.
Compute the level payment on an amortizing loan, the total interest over its life, the first payment's interest and principal split, and the effective annual rate.
Price a plain fixed-coupon bond from its yield, or solve its yield from a declared price, and report Macaulay and modified duration, convexity, DV01 and current yield.

Compute the CAPM cost of equity from a declared risk-free rate, market return and beta, estimating beta from two return series when it is not declared, and relever or unlever it with Hamada when a debt-to-equity ratio is supplied.

Decompose return on equity into net margin, asset turnover and the equity multiplier (and, when EBIT, pre-tax income and tax are declared, the five-step tax- and interest-burden form), with common-size ratios and growth against one declared comparison period.
Apply the mean (or median) of declared comparable multiples to the subject's own earnings, EBITDA, sales or book value, and bridge the result to an equity value and a per-share value.
Measure the cash conversion cycle from receivable, inventory and payable days, and compute the economic order quantity, reorder point and the annualised cost of forgoing a trade discount.
Measure the cash conversion cycle from receivable, inventory and payable days, without the order-quantity and trade-credit terms the combined working-capital method needs.

Combine two assets at a declared weight and report each asset's mean and standard deviation, their covariance and correlation, the portfolio's return and risk, and the Sharpe, beta, Treynor and Jensen performance measures.

Report the profitability index, modified internal rate of return, simple payback and equivalent annual annuity of one declared project alongside its NPV and IRR, so the ranking measures can be compared.
Price a European call or put with Black-Scholes, cross-check it with a binomial tree, and report delta, gamma, vega, theta, rho, intrinsic and time value.
Report parametric and historical value at risk and expected shortfall from a declared return series, with the loss in currency on a declared portfolio value and an optional stress loss.

Apply covered interest parity and relative purchasing power parity to declared spot, interest and inflation rates, report the implied forward, forward premium and real rates, and compare a declared foreign-currency exposure hedged with one forward against the unhedged outcome.

Report earnings per share, the degree of financial leverage, interest cover and the interest tax shield from declared EBIT, interest, tax and shares, add the five-term Altman Z-score when its six figures are declared, and find the EBIT-EPS indifference point against one alternative financing plan.
Recompute a project's NPV at a low and a high discount rate, report the swing, and find the single discount rate at which the decision flips.
Equilibrium price and quantity for declared linear demand and supply curves (Qd = a - bP, Qs = c + dP), with consumer and producer surplus.
Arc (midpoint) price elasticity of demand between two declared price-quantity observations, with the revenue change and an elastic/inelastic classification.
Economic incidence of a declared per-unit tax in a linear partial-equilibrium market: consumer and producer prices, the burden split, tax revenue and deadweight loss.
The effect of a declared price ceiling or floor on a linear competitive market: quantity traded, shortage or surplus, and deadweight loss.
Market concentration from declared firm revenues: Herfindahl-Hirschman index (0-10,000), CR1, CR4 and the equivalent number of equal-sized firms.

Average cost, average variable cost, average fixed cost and marginal cost at a declared quantity for the quadratic cost function TC = fixed + linear x Q + quadratic x Q squared, with optional price, revenue, profit and a shutdown flag.

Profit-maximising quantity and price for a firm facing linear demand P = a - bQ and quadratic cost TC = fixed + linear x Q + quadratic x Q squared, with revenue, cost, profit, markup and the Lerner index.
Markup and Lerner index from a declared price and marginal cost, with the implied demand elasticity under the single-price monopoly model.
GDP by the expenditure approach, plus GNP, NNP, net exports, optional GDP per capita and optional real GDP from a declared deflator.
Total growth, compound annual growth rate and the rule-of-72 doubling time between two declared values, with optional per-capita growth.
Inflation from two CPI values, the exact and approximate real interest rate, and optional real wage growth.
Unemployment rate, labour-force participation rate and employment-population ratio from declared labour-force, employment and working-age population counts.
Simple and currency-adjusted money multipliers from the monetary base, reserve ratio and optional currency drain, with the implied money supply.
Government-spending, tax and balanced-budget multipliers from a declared marginal propensity to consume and proportional tax rate, with the output change from declared fiscal changes.
Overall and primary budget balances, the debt-to-GDP ratio, the interest rate and the standard debt-ratio change from declared budget aggregates.
Market and social optimum under a declared per-unit external cost, with the Pigouvian tax and deadweight loss.
Efficient provision of a public good from two declared linear marginal-benefit schedules and one marginal-cost schedule, with total and net benefit.
Utilitarian, Rawlsian and Nash social welfare from declared incomes, with the selected welfare function.
Gini coefficient, mean, minimum and maximum from declared incomes, with the poorest and richest shares.
Headcount ratio, poverty gap, squared gap and total shortfall from declared incomes and a declared poverty line.
Average tax rate and a simple top-quartile progressivity gap from declared incomes and taxes.
Optimal emissions and pollution tax where declared linear marginal damage equals declared linear marginal abatement cost.
Output gap from actual and potential GDP, with the predicted unemployment change from a declared Okun coefficient.
Ricardian comparative advantage from two countries' declared unit labour requirements in two goods, with opportunity costs and specialisation flags.
Small-country tariff on a linear market: domestic price, imports, tariff revenue and the production and consumption deadweight losses.
Absolute and relative purchasing-power parity from declared price levels and a nominal exchange rate, with the real rate, misalignment and expected depreciation.
Covered interest parity: the implied forward rate and forward premium from a spot rate, two interest rates and a declared horizon, with an optional declared forward and real rates.
Balance-of-payments identity from declared current, capital and financial account balances, with an optional errors term and current-account-to-GDP ratio.
Human Development Index from declared life expectancy, expected and mean years of schooling and GNI per capita, using the UNDP goalposts.
Expected value, expected utility, certainty equivalent and risk premium for a declared gamble under risk neutrality or CRRA utility.
Kahneman-Tversky-style prospect value from declared outcomes, probabilities and a reference point, with loss aversion, curvature and probability weighting.
Real wage, wage share of productivity and optional labour-market tightness - vacancies per unemployed person - from a declared nominal wage, CPI, productivity, vacancy count and unemployment count.
Third-degree price discrimination across two separated linear markets with constant marginal cost: quantities, prices and profit.
Two-firm Cournot equilibrium with linear demand and constant marginal costs: quantities, price and profits.
Two-group, two-period difference-in-differences from four declared means.
Pure-strategy Nash equilibria of a declared 2x2 game, with a flag for each cell and the number of equilibria.
Balanced-panel fixed-effects (within) slope and intercept for one regressor, with within R-squared and degrees of freedom.
Just-identified instrumental-variables slope and intercept with one endogenous regressor and one excluded instrument, plus the first-stage and OLS slopes for comparison.
Sharp regression-discontinuity estimate from a local linear fit on each side of a declared cutoff and bandwidth.
Binary probit with one predictor: latent-index coefficients, log likelihood, McFadden pseudo R-squared and the marginal effect at the mean.
Turn several years of income-statement figures into common-size percentages, an index on the first period, compound growth rates and margin changes.
Top-down TAM, SAM and SOM from a declared population, annual spend and two declared shares, with the customer count implied by the obtainable share.
The start-up funding requirement: declared set-up costs plus working capital plus a declared contingency, less the owner equity and loan already committed, with the amount still to raise.
Months of cash left from a declared opening balance and monthly net cash flow, with optional monthly growth, the lowest balance and the funding gap over a declared horizon.
Cost-plus, target-margin, break-even and target-return prices from declared unit cost, fixed cost, volume and rate inputs.
Return on investment from a declared total investment and net gain, with an annualised return when the holding period is declared.
A period-by-period revenue, cost and profit projection from a declared starting volume, price, unit cost, fixed cost and growth rate.
One priced equity round: post-money value, price per share, new shares, the investor and founder percentages and the dilution, with an optional post-money option pool.
Stage-by-stage conversion and drop-off from the counts you declare, with the overall conversion and, when spend is declared, the acquisition cost per customer.
Pooled retention and churn by period from declared cohort sizes and retained counts, with the average retention and the average lifetime under the declared curve.

A straight line fitted to declared price-quantity observations, with the slope, R-squared, elasticity at the mean price and, when the slope is negative, the revenue-maximising price on the fitted line.
A weighted purchase-intent rate from declared survey counts, with a projected buyer count and revenue when a population and a price are declared.

Click-through, cost per click, cost per thousand impressions, conversion rate, cost per acquisition, return on ad spend and advertising cost of sales from the campaign counts you declare, with break-even return on ad spend when a contribution margin is declared.

A two-proportion comparison of two observed arms: rates, absolute and relative lift, the pooled z-test, a two-sided p-value, an interval for the difference and, when a minimum effect is declared, the visitors each arm would need.
Compare the credit each channel receives under first-click, last-click and linear attribution from the credit counts you declare, and show the largest share disagreement.
Customer acquisition cost, payback, lifetime value and the lifetime-value-to-acquisition-cost ratio for each declared channel, with the blended acquisition cost and each channel's share of spend.
List growth, unsubscribe and bounce rates, open and click rates, click-to-open and revenue per subscriber from the email counts you declare.
Engagement rate, frequency, cost per thousand impressions, cost per engagement, follower growth and engagement per post from the social counts you declare.
Sessions, conversions, conversion rate, revenue per session and channel share from the acquisition rows you declare, with organic-search click-through when impressions and clicks are supplied.
Quintile recency, frequency and monetary scores and the eleven named RFM segments from a declared customer list, with each segment's size and the mean scores.

Reach, reach share, gross impressions, gross rating points, cost per rating point and cost per thousand impressions for each declared vehicle, with the plan total and a combined net reach under random duplication.
Market share, the change from a declared prior period, the implied growth of the firm and the market, penetration against a declared population and relative share against a named largest competitor.
The Risk Priority Number of one FMEA row, the product of its declared severity, occurrence and detection scores.
The total and percentage score of a declared Five-S scorecard, from the criterion scores and the maximum per criterion.

The present value of a customer's margin over a declared horizon, with a constant churn and discount rate, the undiscounted value beside it, and (with an acquisition cost) the value per unit of acquisition cost and the payback period.

Revenue, declared cost, profit, margin and profit share for each segment, product or channel, with the totals, the profitable and unprofitable counts and the smallest number of segments that produce a declared share of the profit.
Material price and usage, labour rate and efficiency, and (when declared) variable and fixed overhead variances for the output actually produced, with a positive figure unfavourable.
Economic order quantity, orders per year, cycle and safety stock, reorder point and the annual ordering and holding cost from declared demand, costs, lead time and a service level.
A multi-server M/M/c queue: utilisation, average customers in the queue and in the system, the average waits, the probability the system is empty and the probability a customer waits.
Process capacity per resource from available hours and minutes per unit, the bottleneck resource and, when demand is declared, each resource's utilisation and the capacity gap.
Critical-path scheduling and PERT from declared activities: early and late dates, total float, the critical path, the project duration and (with three-point estimates) the PERT variance along it.

Level a declared schedule against declared resource capacities: early and levelled starts and finishes, the delay each activity takes, the project duration and the over-capacity periods before and after.
Crash a declared schedule to a target duration: the activity periods bought, the resulting duration and the total crash cost.
Schedule declared activities over a declared working calendar: early and late dates, float, the critical path and the calendar duration with non-working gaps.
Schedule several projects that share declared resources: project and activity starts and finishes, each project's finish and delay against its own CPM, and the overall duration.
Seeded Monte Carlo of a PERT network: mean, P50/P80/P90 and range of the project duration, the share of runs within a target, and each activity's criticality index.
Roll back a declared decision tree: expected value of each alternative, the best alternative, loss probability and the best/worst terminal value for each path.
Value a real option on a declared project value with a Cox-Ross-Rubinstein binomial lattice: option value, intrinsic value, delta, up/down factors and risk-neutral probability.
Score declared alternatives against declared criteria with declared weights: weighted totals, ranks and the best alternative.

A seeded Monte Carlo for two declared decision models: NPV of uncertain cash flows, or profit from uncertain price, variable cost and volume. Reports the mean, P10/P50/P90, range and the share of positive outcomes.

Earned value at a status date: schedule and cost variances, SPI and CPI, one declared estimate at completion, the estimate to complete, the variance at completion and the to-complete performance index.
Overall equipment effectiveness from declared planned time, downtime, ideal cycle time and unit counts: availability, performance, quality and the product of the three.

An individuals chart with moving ranges: mean, estimated sigma, three-sigma control limits, out-of-control points, the longest run on one side of the mean and, when specification limits are declared, Cp and Cpk.
Activity-based costing: a rate per activity from its pool and driver total, each product's allocation from the driver quantities it consumes, and the resulting unit cost.
Sales price, mix and yield variances for two or more products, at budgeted prices with the budget mix as the standard, reconciling to the total revenue change.
Assign declared tasks to stations at a declared cycle time using a declared heuristic (longest task time or ranked positional weight), with the theoretical lower bound, idle time and line efficiency.
Income tax, VAT payable and deferred tax from the rates and figures you declare, with the after-tax income and the total tax charge.

Reconcile a declared accounting profit to taxable income through declared non-deductible, non-taxable and allowance items, then compute current tax, deferred tax, the total tax expense, the effective rate and VAT payable from declared figures.
A depreciation schedule by straight line or declining balance, with the period charge, accumulated depreciation and carrying amount.

Projected income statement, cash flow and balance sheet from declared revenue, margin, costs, depreciation, interest and principal (or a declared opening loan), tax and working-capital days, with the balance check.
Target revenue and units from a declared market size, target share and price, so the market section and the financial plan agree.
A one- or two-way profit table across declared price and volume changes, with the base case, for the plan's risk section.
Value a dated portfolio snapshot from declared holdings, prices and cash: NAV, invested value, cash share, holding weights and concentration.
Measure the time-weighted return of a portfolio across dated periods from each period's start and end NAV, its external flow and, optionally, a declared benchmark level.
